```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
source("helpers.R")
library(patchwork)
```

This file runs every step of the pipeline shown in class. It uses only free packages: **SpATS** for the spatial model of each trial and **lme4** for the multi-environment model.

## The path of the data

```{r flow, fig.width=10, fig.height=3.6}
plot_flow()
```

## 1. Import the data

One row per plot. Key columns: `trial_name`, `accession_name` (clone), `rep_number`, `row_number`, `col_number`, `check_test`, and the traits.

```{r import}
d <- load_cassava("data/cassava_DVGXE_tidy.csv")
dim(d)
table(d$trial, d$check_test)
```

## 2. Pre-processing and quality control

### Field design

```{r design, fig.width=11, fig.height=4.6}
plot_layout_grid(d, c("ciat21", "momi21", "polo21", "repe21", "ciat22", "saha22"))
```

Try the other trials: `arem22`, `cere22`, `stom22`.

### Missing data

Rule of thumb: drop a trait or trial with more than 20% missing.

```{r missing, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.4}
plot_missing(d)
```

### Shared clones

```{r shared, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.4}
plot_connect(d)
```

### Variation between trials

```{r boxplot, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.2}
plot_trait_trial(d, "yield_ha")
```

Try another trait. Change `"yield_ha"` for `"DM_gravity"`.

## 3. Single trial analysis (spatial model, SpATS)

```{r spats, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.4}
m1 <- fit_spats(d, "ciat22", "yield_ha")
plot(m1, cex = 0.7)
getHeritability(m1)
```

Heritability of every trait in every trial (a few seconds):

```{r h2, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.2}
H2 <- single_h2(d)
H2$trial <- factor(H2$trial, levels = levels(d$trial))
H2$trait <- factor(H2$trait, levels = TRAITS)
ggplot(H2, aes(trait, trial, fill = h2)) + geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", h2)), size = 3.2) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F3E5D8", high = "#0072B2", limits = c(0, 1), name = "H2") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

A trait with heritability below about 0.1 in a trial should not go into the multi-environment analysis.

## 4. Multi-environment analysis (lme4)

Model: `trait ~ trial + (1 | clone) + (1 | clone:trial)`.

```{r met}
mY <- met_model(d, "yield_ha")
summary(mY)
met_h2(mY, d, "yield_ha")
```

### Genotypic correlation between trials

```{r gcor, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=4.6}
plot_corr(trial_gcor(mY))
```

## 5. Results

### BLUPs of all traits and correlation between traits

```{r blups, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=4.6}
B <- all_blups(d)
head(B)
plot_corr(cor(B[, TRAITS]))
```

### Selection index

Scores used in the original report: yield +10, dry matter +10, plant type -5. We keep the top 20%.

```{r index}
S <- selection_table(B, weights = c(yield_ha = 10, DM_gravity = 10, plant_type = -5), pct = 0.20)
knitr::kable(head(S[, c("rank", "g", "yield_ha", "DM_gravity", "plant_type", "index", "selected")], 15), digits = 2)
```

Change the weights and see how the list changes. For example, give dry matter a score of 20.

## 6. Optional, two stages with weights

In a **two-stage analysis**, stage 1 fits a spatial model in each trial and gives one adjusted mean (BLUE) for each clone and its standard error. Stage 2 fits the multi-environment model on these means, and each mean gets a **weight**, 1 divided by its squared standard error. A mean with a large error counts less.

The function `lmer()` of lme4 has a `weights` argument, but it always estimates the residual variance again. In stage 2 that residual cannot be told apart from the clone by trial variance. The package **nlme** can keep the residual standard deviation fixed at 1 (`sigma = 1`), so the known variance of every mean is used as it is.

```{r two-stage}
library(nlme)
B1 <- stage1_blues(d, "yield_ha")        # stage 1: BLUE and weight of each clone in each trial
head(B1)
m2 <- stage2_met(B1)                     # stage 2: weighted multi-environment model
VarCorr(m2)
```

Compare the clone BLUPs of the two routes (single stage with lme4, two stages with nlme):

```{r compare-routes}
bA <- met_blups(met_model(d, "yield_ha"))
bB <- data.frame(g = rownames(ranef(m2)$g), blup2 = ranef(m2)$g[, 1])
cmp <- merge(bA, bB, by = "g")
cor(cmp$blup, cmp$blup2)                 # close to 1
```
